hints: Notice liquid X has density $800 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$ and liquid Y has density $1200 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$, so Y is 1.5 times denser than X.
Recall that gauge pressure at depth $h$ in a liquid is $p = h\rho g$, so equal pressure needs $h_X \rho_X = h_Y \rho_Y$ with the same $g$.
Compare the product of density and depth in $\text{m}$ for each pair, and look for the pair where the less dense liquid X has the proportionally larger depth.
walkthrough: Identify the given densities: $\rho_X = 800 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$ and $\rho_Y = 1200 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$, and the depths $h_X$ and $h_Y$ listed in the table.
State the governing rule: pressure due to a liquid column is $p = h\rho g$, plus the same atmospheric pressure at the surface of both large open tanks.
For equal total pressures, set the liquid pressures equal: $h_X \rho_X g = h_Y \rho_Y g$, so $h_X \rho_X = h_Y \rho_Y$.
Rearrange for the depth ratio: $h_X / h_Y = \rho_Y / \rho_X = 1200 / 800 = 1.5$, so the depth in X must be 1.5 times the depth in Y.
Check the table: only $15 \text{ m}$ in X and $10 \text{ m}$ in Y gives $15/10 = 1.5$ and $800 \times 15 = 12000$ equals $1200 \times 10 = 12000$.
